summary: Families that agree on politics talk about it freely, and the ones that disagree mostly stay quiet at the table.
realLife: A Pew survey in November 2018 found 59 percent of adults said their family was fine talking about politics and 40 percent tried to avoid it. Where almost everyone in the family shared the respondent's views, 82 percent were comfortable, and where almost no one did, 28 percent were. About 64 percent said most or all of their family shared their views, and the partisan gap in this was small.
sources: https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2018/11/20/most-say-their-family-is-ok-with-discussing-politics-but-it-helps-if-the-family-agrees/ (Pew Research Center short read on family talk about politics)
